environments.rationale: shared CI is suitable for bounded smoke budgets but too noisy to claim tight relative performance superiority

targets.workload_description: Deterministic in-process projection of one prevalidated tenant/environment context envelope, measured by a standard-library-only runtime probe that excludes build and process-startup time from the reported per-operation latency.
targets.rationale: The runtime now exists and is verified, so the coarse shared-CI absolute p95 ceiling can execute on PRs that touch the pilot runtime while retaining on-demand execution. Shared CI still makes no relative-performance claim.

targets.workload_description: Deterministic in-process validation of one tenant/time/source/permission/provenance Event Search envelope. The standard-library-only runtime is executable; build and process-startup time are excluded from the reported per-operation latency.
targets.rationale: The bounded Event Search validation runtime is executable. The 1 ms shared-CI ceiling applies only to deterministic in-process envelope validation, not backend search latency and not a production Search SLO.

targets.workload_description: Deterministic in-process Search Job orchestration from queued through running to completed against a no-op backend that only acknowledges validated sources. Job creation, build/process startup and backend work are excluded from the reported per-operation latency.
targets.rationale: The 1 ms shared-CI ceiling applies only to backend-neutral Search Job orchestration overhead. It is separate from Event Search validation latency, excludes backend execution, and is not a production search SLO.

targets.workload_description: First-party Event Search frontend local deep-link normalization and bounded incremental result-render update overhead measured by the real ES-module runtime under Node 24.21.0. The probe excludes Node process startup, backend search execution, network transport and browser paint/layout.
targets.rationale: A 16 ms coarse upper bound reserves one 60 Hz frame for local Event Search state/render overhead. The implemented first-party runtime can now execute this deterministic PR/on-demand probe. The measurement excludes backend/network/browser paint and is not a production Search SLO.
